originalTitle: DMart Q1 results: Cons PAT up 11% to Rs 860 crore, revenue rises to Rs 18,795 crore
simplifiedContent: Avenue Supermarts, the company that owns DMart, just released its financial results for the first quarter of the year. The company made a profit of Rs 860 crore, which is 11% more than it made during the same time last year. The company's total sales, or revenue, also increased by 14.9% compared to last year, reaching Rs 18,795 crore. This increase in sales and profit is a good sign for the company, and its expenses were manageable, with a slight improvement in its profit margin. This news is important because it shows how well the company is doing, which can affect its stock price and attract investors.

originalTitle: Nearly 60% of foreign inflows into India-focused funds withdrawn since 2024 peak: Report
simplifiedContent: Foreign investors have taken out almost 60% of the money they had put into funds that focus on India's stock market since the peak in 2024. This means they are pulling their money out of India and putting it elsewhere. About $9 billion was withdrawn from India-focused funds in 2026, showing a significant shift in where investors want to put their money. This matters because it can affect the Indian stock market and economy. The money is being moved to other investments, such as those related to artificial intelligence and US equities, which are currently more attractive to investors.

originalTitle: George Goodman’s investing wisdom: Why sometimes the best move is to do nothing
simplifiedContent: A well-known investor, George Goodman, wrote a book that emphasizes the importance of understanding yourself and your emotions when making investment decisions. He advises against following the crowd and acting impulsively, instead suggesting that being patient and doing nothing can sometimes be the best choice. Goodman's idea is that many people let greed and fear control their decisions, leading them to buy stocks when they're expensive and sell when they're cheap. This approach can help investors make better decisions and avoid common mistakes. By following Goodman's insights, investors can navigate the ups and downs of the market more effectively.

originalTitle: Nomura sees 22% upside in Ather Energy. Here's why it's the brokerage's top EV pick
simplifiedContent: Nomura, a company that helps people decide what to invest in, thinks Ather Energy is a good choice to buy. They believe the company's stock price could go up by 22% because many people are expected to start using electric vehicles, which will help Ather Energy grow. This is why Nomura has raised its target price for Ather Energy to ₹1,470. Nomura likes Ather Energy so much that it's their top pick for electric vehicle companies, meaning they think it has the most potential for success. This matters because it could be a good opportunity for investors to make money by buying Ather Energy's stock.

originalTitle: Why large cap and mid cap funds could be the best mutual fund to bet on now, according to Abakkus study
simplifiedContent: A recent study by Abakkus Mutual Fund found that large and mid-cap funds could be a good investment option right now. This is because company earnings are getting better and the prices of these funds are reasonable. The stock market has gone down a bit, which means it could be a good time for long-term investors to get in. This could lead to stock prices increasing as company earnings continue to grow. Overall, this study suggests that large and mid-cap funds might be a good choice for investors looking to put their money into the market.

originalTitle: AI chip fever returns? SK Hynix  share price surges 13% after blockbuster $26.5 billion US listing
simplifiedContent: SK Hynix, a company that makes computer chips, just listed its shares on the US stock market and raised a lot of money - $26.5 billion. As a result, the company's share price jumped up by 13%, which is a big increase. This happened even though the prices of similar companies' shares have been going up and down lately. The main reason for this surge is that investors are very interested in companies that make the chips used in artificial intelligence (AI) technology. This strong interest is driving up the prices of these chips, which is why SK Hynix's share price increased so much.
